use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has initially achieved Active status, or has returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks (12 seconds) has elapsed, unless an override is used for operational necessity.
The C2 JU initially achieves Active status, or returns to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU initially achieves Active status, or returns to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.

claims.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface, in order to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
Determination of the C² JU responsible for reporting the tracked object shall be in accordance with the procedures in the Air, Surface, Land, and Space Surveillance sections.
The reporting of surveillance track information on the interface shall insure that the information on the track is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.
The source of track data shall be provided (Source TN).
A JU reporting a real-time track shall report the position of the track extrapolated to the time of transmission.
Nonreal-time data shall be identified as such and time tags shall be provided, and nonreal-time track positions shall not be extrapolated.
Procedures for reporting J3.2, J3.3, and J3.5 (PTI = 1) messages are followed.

If certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation, the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3 (indicating manually initiated correlation), the correlation shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data indicates any of the following conditions: (1) Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) Different Mode II codes; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1 (unless No Statement).
Differences in position, velocity, or altitude/elevation recognized by a JU are not resolved through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.

The J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is not transmitted when a JU ceases reporting a track because it has relinquished R^2 to another JU, or when that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.

If a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on the remote track, it may automatically purge those tracks after a specific time interval. Under this condition, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.
Common tracking is established, defined as sharing of a common track number and shifting R² between C² JUs.
Each air, surface (maritime), land (ground), and space tracked object is reported by one C² JU while other C² JUs withhold their reports to prevent cluttering the tactical plot.
Occurrences and duration of dual designations are minimized.
If a dual designation resolution was initiated, the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped are identified.
